name: Bräus Gotland
description: Bräus is an unusual partnership trick-taking game from the Swedish island of Gotland, played by two teams of two or three using a 36-card pack stripped from the standard deck.
deck: 36 cards (2–5 removed from a standard French-suited deck)

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Sweden (Gotland)
Time Period: Medieval roots via the Karnöffel family; modern Gotland rules documented in the late 20th century.
Historical Development: Local descendant of the German Karnöffel group, adapted and preserved as a regional partnership game on Gotland.
Cultural Significance: Traditional island game still played socially in Gotland, showcasing an unusual hierarchy of special cards and sevens-as-tricks.
timeline: 15th century: Karnöffel group of trump games attested in German sources.
20th century: Local Gotland rules for Bräus recorded and translated into English.
Present: Played on Gotland as a traditional partnership game using a 36-card pack.

scoring.description: Each deal awards one point to the team that first reaches six tricks, or two points for Jan when the first six tricks are won in a row; other deals with no decisive result score nothing.
scoring.winCondition: Play deals until one partnership reaches the agreed number of points; the team with the higher total score wins the game.
